registeredBy: Sam (owner); registered on his instruction to close the predictive econometrics gaps, before any run of this test
hypothesis: A random forest nowcast of quarterly real GDP growth (q/q), made 30 days after the quarter ends from the same up-to-ten published predictors as the ridge and lasso nowcasts (300 trees, depth at most 6, leaves of at least 5 quarters, a third of the predictors tried at each split, fixed seed), has a lower RMSE than the historical mean of GDP growth published by then.
knownLimits: Settings fixed before the run, not tuned: with 30 to 70 past quarters per country there is too little data to tune a forest without overfitting the tuning.
Same predictors, lags, countries, quarters, benchmark and pass mark as gdp_nowcast_ridge and gdp_nowcast_lasso.
Bands from the out-of-bag error (each quarter predicted only by trees that did not see it), assumed normal.
